subject: MSA / Order Form — emergency maintenance carveouts and SLO alignment
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Thomas <matthew.thomas@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form — emergency maintenance carveouts and SLO alignment

Hi Matthew,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our procurement team, we reviewed CloudScale's suggested redlines to the MSA/Order Form and wanted to propose a short sync to finalize a couple of operational points before legal does the final pass. The two items we need to resolve now are: uptime SLO targets (and the related credit formula) and emergency maintenance carveouts / P1 response expectations.

Quick context: CloudScale requires 99.95% availability in the order form draft and a capped monthly credit at 30% of fees; your redline asks to limit scheduled maintenance crediting and add a broader emergency maintenance carveout. We should align on language that product/ops can meet while keeping our legal's exposure within acceptable bounds.

Proposed next steps:
- Irene, can you propose compromise language for emergency maintenance carveouts (example: advance notice + mitigation plan + limited emergency maintenance credit cap)?
- Karthik, can ops confirm whether a 6-hour emergency maintenance window with maximum 2 planned instances per quarter is feasible and how that changes our mean-time-to-recover (MTTR) and P1 response SLA?
- Matthew / Procurement, if you can share the specific credit calculation you prefer we can map it to our template and show numerical examples.

Attaching a short support SLO summary that maps typical customer-impact scenarios to our response tiers. I'll also attach the redlined MSA we've been iterating on.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Matthew Thomas <matthew.thomas@cloudscale.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudscale.com, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@cloudscale.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Mar 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — emergency maintenance carveouts and SLO alignment

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear ask. A few notes from CloudScale side:

1) Uptime target: Our procurement team is comfortable with 99.9% in general, but this particular integration handles customer-facing inference pipelines where we need tighter guarantees. We would accept 99.95% only if the credit formula scales meaningfully (we typically ask for an uncapped or very high cap for sustained outages).

2) Emergency maintenance carveout: We understand the need for emergency maintenance, but we need explicit guardrails. Our counter: emergency maintenance allowed if there is an active incident causing or likely to cause security or data loss, with retrospective report within 24 hours and root-cause within 72 hours. Credits apply if emergency maintenance causes >1 hour of degraded service for customer requests.

3) P1 response: We require initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes and engineering-level response within 1 hour for P1s during business hours; 30 minutes and 2 hours outside of business hours.

I'm looping Alyssa (Platform Owner) to confirm whether we can accept a quarterly limit on planned maintenance and to see if they can be flexible on credit caps once we see numerical examples.

Matthew
Matthew Thomas
Senior Counsel, CloudScale Inc.
[matthew.thomas@cloudscale.com]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Mar 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA / Order Form — emergency maintenance carveouts and SLO alignment

Vanessa / Karthik —

Thanks, Matthew. High level legal stance: we can accept a narrowly scoped emergency maintenance carveout provided the text includes (a) strict definition of "emergency" (security, data loss, imminent system failure), (b) required notification windows (immediate notice + 24h retrospective), (c) documented mitigation plan and RCA, and (d) an explicit cap on credit liability that scales with ARR (example clause: maximum aggregate credits in any 30-day period shall not exceed 40% of monthly recurring fees for the affected service).

Open questions for ops/product: can we include automated throttling/prefix-cache isolations as required mitigations in the clause (that is, if ops can route traffic away or cache customer prefixes, that should reduce crediting)? Also, what normal MTTR assumptions should be reflected in the P1 response language?

I propose the following compromise language block for the emergency carveout (high level, draft):
"Emergency maintenance" means maintenance reasonably necessary to address an imminent security vulnerability or system condition likely to cause data loss or widespread service interruption. Provider will: (1) provide immediate notification to Customer within one hour of commencement; (2) deliver a retrospective report within 24 hours and a root cause analysis within 72 hours; (3) implement reasonable mitigations to reduce customer impact. Provider's aggregate liability for emergency maintenance-related credits is capped at the greater of 40% of the monthly fee for the affected service or one monthly invoice.

Please confirm ops feasibility — Karthik? If feasible, I'll draft a legal-friendly redline and push to DocuSign once CloudScale signs off on numeric examples.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA / Order Form — emergency maintenance carveouts and SLO alignment

Irene / Vanessa —

Operational reality: we can accept the emergency definition Irene proposed and meet the notification and RCA windows. A few practical constraints to call out so legal can phrase appropriately:

- Emergency maintenance — feasible as long as team has permission to pre-empt non-critical workloads. We recommend limiting "emergency" to conditions that threaten data integrity or service continuity; otherwise the clause gets abused.
- Timing: immediate notification within 1 hour is doable; retrospective 24h and RCA in 72h are tight but acceptable as "best reasonable efforts" with exceptions for complex incidents. Put "best reasonable efforts" language on timelines.
- P1 response: acknowledgement within 15 minutes is tough at scale unless we guarantee a dedicated engineering on-call for CloudScale; we can commit to acknowledgement in 30 minutes and engineering-level mitigation start within 1 hour during business hours (8am–6pm PT). Outside business hours: acknowledgement in 60 minutes and mitigation start within 2 hours. If CloudScale requires 15/1h globally we need a premium support add-on (we can scope pricing).
- Credits: we can run the numeric examples — likely the 40% cap Irene proposed for emergency maintenance looks workable, but uncapped credits for sustained outages is a non-starter. Suggest tying credit tiers to % monthly downtime with a multiplier table (examples in the attached PDF).

I'll attach a one-page ops note mapping each legalable commitment to operational action items. If the customer wants 15-minute ack globally, let's surface the premium support pricing.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.ai]
[attachment: ops-commitments-mapping.pdf (pdf)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Thomas <matthew.thomas@cloudscale.com>, procurement@cloudscale.com, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA / Order Form — emergency maintenance carveouts and SLO alignment

Matthew / Alyssa / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per the internal review above, summary proposal for your team to review:

- Uptime SLO: Provider agrees to 99.95% availability for the billed inference endpoint.
- Credits: Tied to monthly downtime percentage with tiers (example: 99.9–99.95 => 10% credit; 99.0–99.9 => 25% credit; <99.0 => 40% credit), with the provider's aggregate credit liability capped at the greater of 40% of monthly fees or one monthly invoice for emergency maintenance events.
- Emergency maintenance: Allowed for security/data-loss/system integrity scenarios only; Provider will notify within 1 hour of commencement, provide a retrospective within 24h and RCA within 72h (best reasonable efforts).
- P1 response: Acknowledgement within 30 minutes and engineering mitigation start within 1 hour during business hours (8am–6pm PT). Outside business hours: acknowledgement within 60 minutes and mitigation start within 2 hours. If CloudScale requires 15-minute global ack, we can provide via premium support add-on (pricing TBD).
- Maintenance windows: Planned maintenance will be limited to two occurrences per quarter per region with advanced notice (72h) and will not exceed 4 hours each unless mutually agreed.

Next steps:
1) Matthew / Alyssa — please confirm whether these terms are acceptable in principle or identify specific numeric changes (credit tiers or caps).
2) Irene will prepare a redline for the MSA (will attach to DocuSign) once we have numeric confirmation.
3) Vanessa will schedule a 30-min legal/ops sync if needed (I can do Tues/Thurs mornings PT).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week if possible.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
